The MBR combines a suspended growth biological reactor for activated sludge treatment with submerged membranes for solids separation.
A deoxygenation (deox) zone is located upstream of the anoxic zone.

The next treatment stage of the MBR process is the anoxic zone... to promote the oxidation of dissolved nitrates into nitrogen gas which is removed to the atmosphere, a process called denitrification.

The aeration zone will be equipped with fine bubble diffusers... to promote a suspended biological growth that breaks down the soluble BOD... and promote growth of nitrifying bacteria, which oxidize ammonia into nitrates – a process called nitrification.
The aeration basins overflow into post-anoxic basins, which are designed to further enhance the denitrification process.
The selected Zenon membrane configuration will consist of hollow fiber ultrafiltration membranes... The immersed membranes separate the solids from the MBR effluent, called permeate.
Sodium hypochlorite will be used to dose stored permeate in a backwash tank.
A slight vacuum will be applied to the permeate header by a centrifugal pump... the permeate will flow through the pump to the downstream processes.
Six axial flow pumps (5 duty, 1 standby) will be used to provide a flow up to 6Q... The mixed liquor recirculation pumps will be VFD driven for flow control.
Aeration air will be provided to the system by high-speed turbocompressors... Four separate high-speed turbocompressors... will supply the membrane agitation air.
Disinfection of the portion of the MBR effluent used for recycled water will be accomplished by chlorination.
An aboveground, fuel-type storage tank and gear pumps are used for storage and feed of the methanol.
